paper.title: Normal and pathogenic variation of RFC1 repeat expansions: implications for clinical diagnosis

persona.role: Rare-disease repeat-expansion researcher or laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research interpretation after an adult-onset ataxia workup

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow uses a population reference to ask whether a comparable represented state occurs. It does not classify an individual's allele or make a diagnosis.

startingState.trigger: An externally characterized RFC1 repeat result with motif, approximate size, zygosity, and assay limitations.
inputs: Compatible research phenotype and RFC1 locus
GRCh38 coordinates, or a documented mapping to GRCh38
RP-PCR, Southern blot, OGM, or targeted long-read result
Motif, approximate size, interruptions, second allele, tissue, and uncertainty
startingState.question: Does this release contain comparable size, sequence-configuration, and local-haplotype states with adequate callability?
startingState.stopRule: If only a positive RP-PCR result is known and allele structure is missing, stop: the population browser cannot reconstruct it.

before: Record assay, tissue, build, motif spelling, total repeat units, interruptions, second allele, and uncertainty.
Normalize to the browser locus while retaining the original notation; do not turn paper observations into a universal size threshold.
inside: Open the RFC1 region with HGSVC/HPRC haplotypes and confirm GRCh38/Y1 provenance.
Inspect all alleles from one source event rather than treating normalized insertions as independent loci.
Compare length, exact sequence or motif decomposition, interruptions, global and stratum AC/AN, and carrier chromosome copies; treat the paper's 66 kb haplotype as a separate comparison.
after: Record the matching rule, callable denominator, missingness, release, run, and browser state.
Hand allele-level evidence to the research team for segregation, orthogonal sizing, phenotype review, and interpretation outside the browser.

paper.title: Optimized testing strategy for the diagnosis of GAA- FGF14 ataxia

persona.context: Research comparison after an externally performed FGF14 sizing and sequence assay

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This workflow asks whether a comparable sequence-resolved reference allele is represented and with what callable denominator. It cannot diagnose an individual, classify an allele, transfer the paper's threshold or calibration, or infer pathogenicity or benignity from population occurrence or absence.

startingState.trigger: An external FGF14 result with an allele pair, assay-specific size estimate, and preferably bidirectional motif or sequence information.
inputs: Original assay and laboratory: fLR-PCR/capillary electrophoresis, gel sizing, bidirectional RP-PCR, Sanger sequencing, nanopore sequencing, or another declared method
Raw allele-size estimate and any locally calibrated estimate, kept as separate values with control/calibration provenance
Both alleles, cyclic motif spelling, 5′ and 3′ interruption or polymorphism information, tissue, and uncertainty
Reference build and a documented mapping to GRCh38 chr13:102161575–102161726
A predeclared matching rule: exact ALT sequence, sequence-decomposed repeat count and interruption pattern, or length-only similarity
Browser release, cohort, source event, global and stratum AC/AN, and missingness/callability fields
startingState.question: Does this release contain an exact-sequence or explicitly weaker length/composition match to the externally characterized FGF14 allele, after keeping assay-specific sizing uncertainty separate?
startingState.stopRule: Stop exact comparison if the build, assay basis, allele pair, or sequence/motif evidence is missing; do not convert an uncalibrated capillary estimate with the paper's cohort-specific regression or use the paper's clinical threshold in the browser.

before: Record both alleles, original motif notation, assay, tissue, raw size, locally calibrated size, controls, sequence coverage, interruptions, and uncertainty without replacing the original measurement.

Normalize the locus to GRCh38 chr13:102161575–102161726 while retaining the source coordinates; bridge it to source event chr13-102161564-TRV-280 rather than treating the event's 281 bp reference span as the repeat tract.
Choose and label the matching rule before looking at population data: exact sequence is strongest; length-only similarity must remain a weaker result.
inside: Open chr13:102111564–102211564 with HGSVC/HPRC and verify dataset, cohort, reference build, accepted Y1 source, run, and chromosome scope.
Select all ALT records sharing source_variant_id chr13-102161564-TRV-280; do not interpret its normalized alleles as independent loci.

Compare the external allele to exact ALT sequence and event-level base-pair difference only on the declared basis; never silently equate event length with GAA repeat count or apply the paper's fLR-PCR correction.
For any candidate match, retain global and ancestry/sex-stratum AC/AN and the exact allele ID; distinguish an exact sequence match from same-length but structurally unresolved alleles.

Inspect motif, interruption, purity, full-cohort repeat-count distribution, and chromosome-copy linkage availability. If fields are empty or unavailable, report the corresponding comparison as data-blocked rather than absent.
after: Return one bounded outcome: exact-sequence represented, length-only represented, not observed in representation-complete callable data, or representation/data blocked.

Record the matching rule, external assay basis, raw and locally calibrated values, source event and allele ID, AC/AN by reported stratum, missingness, release/run, evidence date, and browser/API query state.
Hand the reference observation to the research or laboratory team for orthogonal sizing, segregation, phenotype review, and interpretation outside the browser.

branches.condition: Build, assay basis, second allele, or motif/sequence evidence is missing
branches.action: Stop exact comparison and request the missing source result; do not reconstruct an allele from a positive RP-PCR or a single size number.

branches.condition: Only an uncalibrated fLR-PCR/capillary size is available
branches.action: Preserve it as assay-specific and uncertain; do not apply the paper's regression or threshold as a universal conversion.

branches.condition: An exact ALT sequence match is represented with explicit AC/AN
branches.action: Report the allele ID, matching rule, AC/AN, strata, and provenance as population-reference occurrence only.

branches.condition: Only event-level length is similar while motif, purity, or interruptions are unresolved
branches.action: Report length-only similarity and mark structural equivalence data-blocked; do not call the alleles comparable in sequence.

branches.condition: No candidate match is returned but sequence representation, distribution, or callability is incomplete
branches.action: Report unanswerable/data-blocked rather than zero or absent.

branches.condition: No candidate match is observed in representation-complete callable data
branches.action: Report not observed with the exact denominator and release; this is not evidence of pathogenicity.

paper.title: Accurate long-read sequencing identified GBA1 as major risk factor in the Luxembourgish Parkinson’s study

locus: GBA1/GBA1LP (GBAP1) · GBA1 chr1:155,234,452–155,244,699; GBA1LP chr1:155,213,821–155,227,574 (GRCh38, pinned browser annotation)

persona.role: Neurogenetics researcher or molecular laboratory scientist
persona.context: Research review of a GBA1 call or recombinant-like marker set at a locus where the pseudogene and complex structures can confound copy assignment

nonDiagnosticBoundary: This population-reference workflow can ask whether a comparable copy-assigned sequence or structural state is represented. It cannot diagnose Parkinson’s or Gaucher disease, classify an allele, or transfer the paper’s Parkinson’s disease odds ratios to HGSVC/HPRC participants.

startingState.trigger: An externally normalized GBA1/GBAP1 variant set, conversion-like tract, hybrid, or duplication hypothesis with assay and phase evidence.
inputs: Original HGVS/protein notation, transcript, reference build, strand, and normalization receipt; retain the paper’s GRCh37/NM_001005742 notation separately from GRCh38 browser coordinates
Assay type and blind spots, including primer coordinates, amplification specificity, coverage, allele dropout, size-selection limits, and whether GBAP1 was sequenced
Per-chromosome sequence or assembly path spanning unique flanks, all GBA-related copies, and the inter-copy interval
Pinned GBA1 and GBAP1/GBA1LP reference sequences plus a versioned panel of paralog-diagnostic markers
Copy number, order, orientation, breakpoint intervals, phased small variants, unresolved bases, and confidence
startingState.question: Can each observed variant or donor-like tract be assigned to a specific GBA1, GBAP1, hybrid, duplicated, or unresolved physical copy on one chromosome, and is a comparable callable structural haplotype represented in this release?
startingState.stopRule: If evidence consists only of the paper’s GBA1-specific amplicon, a flat SNV list, or a generic DEL/INS/DUP overlap without unique-flank anchors and a diagnostic-marker path, stop before assigning GBAP1, conversion boundaries, hybrid identity, copy order, or duplication origin.

before: Preserve the source assay result exactly, then normalize each small variant and breakpoint to GRCh38 while retaining original build/transcript notation and a mapping receipt; protein labels alone are not browser queries.

Pin locus annotation and reference sequences. The checked browser annotation is GBA1 ENSG00000177628.16 at chr1:155234452–155244699 and GBA1LP ENSG00000160766.15, gencode symbol GBAP1, at chr1:155213821–155227574; both are on the minus strand.

Build a chromosome-level evidence object from unique left/right flanks through every GBA-related segment. Record physical copy count, order, orientation, gaps, local assembly/read support, and a versioned set of GBA1-versus-GBAP1 diagnostic markers.

Predeclare matching levels: exact sequence-and-path match; same copy class with different tract boundary; marker-similar only; generic interval overlap; unresolved. Do not let generic overlap satisfy a copy-identity match.
inside: Open chr1:155200000–155300000 with HGSVC/HPRC haplotypes and confirm GRCh38/Y1 provenance, the pinned gene models, cohort, run, and chromosome-wide source identity.

Select one sample strand at a time and require unique-flank anchors before interpreting the linear variant rows. Compare its sequence simultaneously against the pinned GBA1 and GBAP1 references rather than assigning origin from genomic overlap alone.

Lay out every physical segment in chromosome order and orientation. Label a canonical GBA1 or GBAP1 copy only when its flanks and diagnostic-marker majority agree; retain conflicting or uncovered segments as unresolved.

Call a conversion-like tract only on an anchored recipient copy when a contiguous run of donor-paralog diagnostic markers is bounded on both sides by recipient markers. Report the tract as an interval between the nearest informative markers, with marker count, conflicts, coverage, and uncertainty; do not convert it into an exact breakpoint.

Call a hybrid candidate only when one physical copy has a supported transition in backbone/paralog identity with a junction interval. Call a duplication only when the chromosome path contains an extra physical copy; assign that copy’s GBA1-like, GBAP1-like, hybrid, or unresolved origin independently and preserve copy order.

Assign small variants only after copy identity. A RecNciI-like marker pattern requires p.L483P, p.A495P, and p.V499V in cis on the same GBA1-assigned copy after build/transcript normalization. The three markers alone do not establish conversion boundaries, a reciprocal product, or a locus-spanning structural mechanism.

Group copies into structural classes only after representation reconciliation. For each class show exact-match count, callable chromosome-haplotype denominator, unresolved/no-call count, participants represented, sampling-group strata, release/run, matching rule, and query receipt.
after: Export a machine-readable per-chromosome path: participant, sample strand, unique-flank anchors, ordered segments, copy labels, orientation, diagnostic markers, tract/junction intervals, linked variants, confidence, unresolved sequence, matching level, and provenance.

Use orthogonal locus-specific sequencing, breakpoint validation, or assembly review for candidate hybrids, duplications, and conversion tracts; use segregation, phenotype, and expert interpretation outside the population browser.

Report only observed, not observed in callable copies, representation mismatch, or data-blocked. Keep the paper’s 77/637 versus 34/675 and OR 2.6 (1.6–4.1) confined to its filtered clinical case-control cohort.

branches.action: Assign small variants to the supported physical copy and report the two-copy chromosome path with callable-copy evidence.

For an exact match, report global and XX/XY-stratified AC/AN, callable chromosome copies, no-call copies, participants, and the ploidy rule. XX contributes at most two non-PAR X copies and XY at most one; observed VCF AN is not a substitute for event callability.
If no exact row is found, inspect spanning-read/junction and breakpoint-flank callability for every eligible copy. Base-depth coverage alone cannot certify a 2.876 kb deletion as callable.

acceptanceTest.fixture: GRCh38 chrX non-PAR fixtures containing: (A) the exact 2,876 bp deletion in a junction-confirmed XX copy; (B) a coordinate-shifted but junction-identical Alu representation; (C) an overlapping 3.3 kb deletion with a different junction; (D) callable XX and XY reference copies plus explicit no-call copies; and (E) pinned and unpinned JASPAR/GTEx/RegulomeDB snapshots.
acceptanceTest.actions: Open the region, verify provenance, search paper endpoints and junction, normalize A/B, compare C, audit X-ploidy/event callability, toggle regulatory evidence, and export the receipt.
acceptanceTest.expected: A and B collapse to one exact event; C remains candidate overlap; AC/AN equals callable non-PAR X copies with XX/XY and no-call counts shown; the no-event state is not observed only when D is complete; E displays build/release/feature/tissue/effect provenance and marks unpinned evidence unavailable; the export reproduces all identities and counts.
acceptanceTest.forbidden: The result must not count participants as chromosome copies, treat aggregate depth as deletion callability, call an overlap exact, turn missing data into zero, use population occurrence/absence to validate regulatory effect, or label the deletion pathogenic, benign, causal, or diagnostic.

evidence.claim: The paper reports an hg38 hemizygous SLC16A2 intron-1 deletion at chrX:74,460,691–74,463,566; the inclusive span is 2,876 bp.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 3 and 7; Fig. 3 caption, p. 16

evidence.claim: Multiplex PCR in the family showed the deletion allele in both affected males and their carrier mother, while the father had only the wild-type allele; Sanger sequencing of the deleted-allele PCR product established the breakpoints.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 4–7; Fig. 1 caption, p. 14; Fig. 2 caption, p. 15

evidence.claim: Figure 2A displays the breakpoint trace AGACGGAGTCTGGCTCTGTCG|CCCAGGCTGGAGTGCAGTGGCA; AluY1 and AluY2 flank the event and the figure reports 266/304 bases (87.50%) similarity.
evidence.citation: Manual transcription of PDF Fig. 2, p. 15; requires second-person sequence review before publication

evidence.claim: JASPAR 2022 predictions include STAT2, RORA, RORC, ZIC1::ZIC2, FOXD3 and zinc-finger binding sites; RORA/RORC sites overlap a 30-mammal conserved region.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 7–8, Table 1; Fig. 3 caption, p. 16

evidence.claim: The paper reports rs1263181 as a GTEx eQTL across 49 tissues, with skeletal-muscle NES +0.07 (P=2.9×10^-3), thyroid NES -0.08 (P=3.0×10^-4), and no significant effect in blood or skin; it also reports RegulomeDB category 1.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 7 and 10; Fig. 4 caption, p. 17

evidence.claim: Blood RT-PCR found no aberrant exon-1-to-exon-2 splicing, and the authors explicitly state that no functional study established a direct causal link; ACMG/ClinGen classification remained VUS.
evidence.citation: PDF pp. 7 and 10

evidence.claim: The paper's population comparisons found no exact case in gnomAD SV v4.0, two larger overlapping female-carrier singleton deletions, no overlapping hemizygous deletion among 15,073 males, and no SLC16A2-overlapping deletion among 1,094 Korean genomes.
evidence.citation: PDF p. 6

evidence.claim: A reproducible recurrence workflow must canonicalize the deleted-base interval to retained flanks and junction sequence because Alu microhomology can shift equivalent VCF coordinates; overlap or a shared anchor is insufficient.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction from paper Fig. 2 and current source-event contract; requires workflow review

evidence.claim: At this non-PAR X locus, the denominator must count callable chromosome copies under explicit ploidy (up to two per XX participant and one per XY participant) and must expose no-call copies; participant N and neighboring-variant AN are not substitutes.
evidence.citation: Analyst reconstruction; requires data-semantics review
